questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with right flank pain and gross hematuria for one week. Renal ultrasound reveals a solid mass in her right kidney rather than the suspected kidney stone. Which malignancy is most likely?
explanations: Incorrect. Transitional cell carcinoma typically arises from the renal pelvis or ureter, not the renal parenchyma.
Correct. RCC is the most common primary renal malignancy of adults and classically presents with hematuria and a solid renal mass.
Incorrect. Wilms tumor is a pediatric renal tumor, not an adult malignancy.
Incorrect. Primary renal lymphoma is rare and not the most common renal mass in an adult.
Incorrect. Squamous cell carcinoma of the kidney is rare and linked to chronic irritation, not this presentation.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history is diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma. Which risk factor is the most significant modifiable contributor to his disease?
explanations: Incorrect. Hypertension is a risk factor but not the most significant.
Incorrect. Obesity contributes to RCC risk but is not the most significant.
Correct. Tobacco use is the most significant risk factor; smoking doubles the incidence of RCC.
Incorrect. Family history matters but is not the leading risk factor.
Incorrect. Asbestos is an occupational risk factor but not the most significant overall.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with painless gross hematuria, right flank pain, and a palpable right flank mass. He is otherwise asymptomatic. This presentation is known as the classic triad of which condition?
explanations: Incorrect. Bladder cancer presents with hematuria but not flank mass and flank pain as a classic triad.
Correct. The classic triad of hematuria, flank pain, and palpable flank mass is the textbook RCC presentation but occurs in only ~10% of cases.
Incorrect. PKD presents with bilateral cystic kidneys and hypertension, not this triad.
Incorrect. Pyelonephritis presents with fever, dysuria, and CVA tenderness.
Incorrect. Stones cause colicky pain and hematuria but not a palpable mass.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with newly diagnosed renal cell carcinoma is being counseled on the histologic types. Which subtype accounts for the majority of cases?
explanations: Incorrect. Papillary carcinoma accounts for ~15% of RCCs.
Incorrect. Chromophobe carcinoma is the least common at ~5%.
Correct. Clear cell carcinoma is the most common subtype, accounting for ~70% of RCCs.
Incorrect. Collecting duct carcinoma is rare and not among the three main subtypes.
Incorrect. Medullary carcinoma is rare and associated with sickle cell trait.

questions.stem: A pathologist examines a nephrectomy specimen and describes a golden-yellow tumor in the upper pole with areas of hemorrhage and necrosis. Microscopy shows nests of cells with clear cytoplasm. From which structure does this tumor arise?
explanations: Incorrect. The distal convoluted tubule gives rise to papillary RCC, not clear cell.
Incorrect. Intercalated cells of collecting ducts give rise to chromophobe carcinoma.
Incorrect. Podocytes do not give rise to RCC.
Correct. Clear cell carcinoma arises from the proximal tubular epithelium; the yellow color is from intracellular lipid accumulation.
Incorrect. The loop of Henle is not the origin of clear cell RCC.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is found to have bilateral renal masses, retinal angiomas, and a cerebellar hemangioblastoma. Loss of which chromosome region is most likely responsible?
explanations: Correct. Loss of the short arm (3p) contains the VHL gene locus and underlies clear cell RCC and von Hippel-Lindau disease.
Incorrect. 5q deletions are associated with myelodysplastic syndromes, not RCC.
Incorrect. 17p contains TP53 but is not the VHL locus.
Incorrect. 11p contains the WT1 gene associated with Wilms tumor.
Incorrect. 22q is associated with NF2 and DiGeorge syndrome.

questions.stem: A medical student is studying the molecular biology of clear cell RCC. When the VHL protein is inactive, which transcription factor accumulates and drives oncogenic gene expression?
explanations: Incorrect. p53 is a tumor suppressor not regulated by VHL.
Incorrect. MYC collaborates with HIF in metabolic reprogramming but is not the factor stabilized by VHL loss.
Incorrect. NF-kB is not the transcription factor targeted by the VHL ubiquitin ligase complex.
Correct. VHL normally targets HIF-1 for O2-dependent degradation; when VHL is inactive, HIF-1 accumulates and drives VEGF and IGF-1 expression.
Incorrect. STAT3 is not the substrate of the VHL ubiquitin ligase complex.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with VHL disease is found to have a clear cell renal mass. Loss of VHL function leads to upregulation of which pro-angiogenic factor?
explanations: Correct. HIF-1 accumulation drives VEGF expression, promoting angiogenesis in RCC tumors.
Incorrect. PDGF is not the brick's stated HIF-driven angiogenic factor in RCC.
Incorrect. TGF-beta is involved in fibrosis and immunosuppression, not HIF-driven angiogenesis in RCC.
Incorrect. FGF-2 is angiogenic but not the brick-highlighted HIF target.
Incorrect. Angiotensin II is a vasoconstrictor, not a HIF-induced angiogenic factor.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man undergoes nephrectomy for a renal mass. Pathology shows multifocal bilateral tumors with papillae lined by neoplastic cells, foamy macrophages in the cores, and psammoma bodies. Which oncogene mutation is most associated?
explanations: Incorrect. VHL is associated with clear cell carcinoma, not papillary.
Correct. Papillary RCC arises from the distal convoluted tubule and is associated with MET oncogene mutations.
Incorrect. RET mutations underlie MEN2 and medullary thyroid cancer.
Incorrect. BRAF is associated with melanoma and colorectal cancers.
Incorrect. KRAS is associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers, not papillary RCC.

questions.stem: A nephrectomy specimen shows a small, well-circumscribed tan-brown tumor. Microscopy reveals sheets of pale eosinophilic cells with perinuclear halos. What is the most likely subtype?
explanations: Incorrect. Clear cell carcinoma has clear cytoplasm and a yellow gross appearance.
Incorrect. Papillary carcinoma shows papillary structures with foam cells, not perinuclear halos.
Correct. Chromophobe carcinoma arises from collecting duct intercalated cells and shows pale eosinophilic cells with perinuclear halos.
Incorrect. Oncocytoma is benign and has different histology with abundant mitochondria.
Incorrect. Collecting duct carcinoma is aggressive and rare, with different histology.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with renal cell carcinoma is found to have hypercalcemia despite normal PTH levels and no bone metastases. Which mediator is most likely responsible?
explanations: Incorrect. Calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia occurs in granulomatous disease, not RCC.
Incorrect. Calcitonin lowers calcium and is not the mediator here.
Correct. RCC commonly secretes PTHrP, producing humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy; resolution often signals successful cancer treatment.
Incorrect. Dietary vitamin D excess is not the RCC-related mechanism.
Incorrect. The vignette states there are no bone metastases.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with renal cell carcinoma is found to have hematocrit of 58% with no smoking history or lung disease. Which paraneoplastic mechanism best explains this finding?
explanations: Incorrect. PTHrP causes hypercalcemia, not polycythemia.
Correct. RCC can produce erythropoietin, causing elevated hematocrit (secondary polycythemia).
Incorrect. Cortisol excess causes Cushing features, not polycythemia.
Incorrect. Calcitonin secretion is not an RCC paraneoplastic feature.
Incorrect. ADH excess causes SIADH and hyponatremia, not polycythemia.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with renal cell carcinoma has fatigue and pallor. CBC shows hemoglobin of 9.2 g/dL with normal iron studies. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is most likely?
explanations: Incorrect. Iron studies are normal, ruling out iron deficiency.
Correct. Anemia of chronic disease occurs in 30-90% of RCC patients and is the most common paraneoplastic finding.
Incorrect. Hemolytic anemia would show elevated LDH and indirect bilirubin.
Incorrect. Aplastic anemia causes pancytopenia, not the RCC pattern described.
Incorrect. Pernicious anemia is due to B12 deficiency from intrinsic factor loss.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman presents with hematuria. Workup is concerning for renal cell carcinoma. Which imaging study is the preferred diagnostic test?
explanations: Correct. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis is the preferred study for suspected RCC.
Incorrect. Plain X-ray cannot identify renal masses.
Incorrect. Bone scan is used for metastatic workup, not initial diagnosis.
Incorrect. PET scan is not the preferred initial study for RCC.
Incorrect. MR angiography is not first-line for diagnosis of RCC.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old pregnant woman presents with flank pain and hematuria. A renal mass is suspected. Which imaging study is most appropriate?
explanations: Incorrect. CT with contrast exposes the fetus to radiation and contrast.
Correct. Renal ultrasound is preferred when patients cannot receive radiation (pregnancy) or IV contrast (decreased kidney function).
Incorrect. PET scan uses radiation and is not appropriate in pregnancy.
Incorrect. X-rays use radiation and cannot characterize renal masses.
Incorrect. Bone scan uses radiation and is not the initial test.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed with a 5 cm renal mass on CT, with imaging features highly suspicious for RCC and no metastases. What is the next step in management?
explanations: Incorrect. Biopsy is typically not required because surgical resection provides both diagnosis and cure.
Incorrect. RCC is relatively chemoresistant and chemotherapy is not first-line.
Incorrect. RCC is relatively radioresistant.
Correct. For localized RCC in surgical candidates, surgical resection (partial or radical nephrectomy) is the standard management.
Incorrect. Watchful waiting is only considered in older patients with small tumors who are poor surgical candidates.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man undergoes radical nephrectomy for renal cell carcinoma. Which structures are removed in a radical (as opposed to limited) nephrectomy?
explanations: Incorrect. Removing only the kidney describes a limited (partial) nephrectomy.
Incorrect. The bladder is not removed in a standard radical nephrectomy.
Correct. Radical nephrectomy removes the kidney, the ipsilateral adrenal gland, and nearby lymph nodes.
Incorrect. The contralateral kidney is preserved.
Incorrect. Only the ipsilateral adrenal is removed, not the contralateral.

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man with severe COPD and heart failure has a small renal mass suspicious for RCC. He is not a surgical candidate. Which option is reasonable?
explanations: Correct. Cryotherapy and radiofrequency ablation are ablative procedures used in patients who are not good surgical candidates.
Incorrect. RCC is relatively chemoresistant and high-dose chemotherapy is not standard.
Incorrect. Whole-body radiation is not appropriate therapy.
Incorrect. Bilateral nephrectomy is not indicated for a unilateral mass.
Incorrect. Bone marrow transplant has no role in RCC therapy.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with metastatic RCC is to receive systemic therapy. Which agent is a checkpoint inhibitor targeting PD-1?
explanations: Incorrect. Ipilimumab targets CTLA-4, not PD-1.
Incorrect. Sunitinib is a VEGF/tyrosine kinase inhibitor, not a checkpoint inhibitor.
Incorrect. Axitinib is a VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
Incorrect. Belzutifan is a HIF-2alpha inhibitor.
Correct. Nivolumab is an anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor used in metastatic RCC, often combined with ipilimumab.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with refractory metastatic clear cell RCC is started on belzutifan. What is its mechanism of action?
explanations: Incorrect. PD-1 inhibition describes nivolumab and pembrolizumab.
Incorrect. CTLA-4 inhibition describes ipilimumab.
Incorrect. VEGFR TKI describes axitinib or sunitinib.
Correct. Belzutifan is a HIF-2alpha inhibitor used in refractory RCC; it targets the oncogenic HIF pathway driven by VHL loss.
Incorrect. mTOR inhibition describes everolimus.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with metastatic RCC is treated with high-dose interleukin-2. Which severe toxicity should be monitored for?
explanations: Correct. High-dose IL-2 can cause capillary leak syndrome with hypotension, arrhythmias, renal dysfunction, and multi-organ toxicity.
Incorrect. Pulmonary fibrosis is not the classic IL-2 toxicity highlighted in the brick.
Incorrect. Peripheral neuropathy is more typical of platinum or vinca agents.
Incorrect. Pancreatitis is not the characteristic IL-2 toxicity.
Incorrect. Cardiomyopathy is not the brick's described IL-2 toxicity.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with metastatic RCC undergoes nephrectomy despite having distant metastases. What is the primary rationale?
choices: Preventing recurrence in the other kidney
explanations: Incorrect. Surgery in metastatic disease is not curative.
Correct. Cytoreductive surgery reduces tumor burden in metastatic RCC, an approach unusual for most cancers but used in RCC.
Incorrect. Diagnosis is typically already established by imaging in metastatic disease.
Incorrect. RCC tends to be unilateral and metastasizes hematogenously, not to the contralateral kidney via spread.
Incorrect. Pain control is not the primary rationale for nephrectomy in metastatic disease.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with renal cell carcinoma has imaging showing tumor extending beyond the kidney capsule. Which structure represents the local boundary the tumor may breach first?
explanations: Incorrect. Bowman capsule is a glomerular structure, not a perirenal boundary.
Incorrect. The inner renal capsule sits closer to the parenchyma; Gerota fascia is the perinephric boundary referenced in staging.
Correct. RCC may extend locally through the renal (Gerota) fascia into perinephric fat and into the adrenal gland.
Incorrect. The kidney is retroperitoneal and not bounded by peritoneum directly.
Incorrect. The diaphragm is superior and not the first local boundary breached.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with renal cell carcinoma has metastases on staging workup. RCC is unusual among carcinomas because it preferentially metastasizes via which route?
explanations: Incorrect. Most carcinomas spread lymphatically; RCC is an exception.
Correct. RCC has a predilection for hematogenous over lymphatic spread, which is unique among carcinomas; it commonly metastasizes to lungs, bones, liver, and brain.
Incorrect. Peritoneal seeding is typical of ovarian or gastric cancers.
Incorrect. Perineural invasion is characteristic of pancreatic and prostate cancers.
Incorrect. Transcoelomic spread is not the RCC pattern.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man undergoes nephrectomy revealing clear cell RCC confined to the kidney without metastases. What is his approximate 5-year survival rate?
explanations: Incorrect. 5% survival is far worse than localized RCC outcomes.
Incorrect. 25% is too low for nonmetastatic disease.
Incorrect. 50% is too low for localized RCC.
Incorrect. 70% is the survival rate for metastatic disease, not localized.
Correct. The 5-year survival rate for nonmetastatic RCC is up to 95%; metastatic disease is ~70%.
